name: The Bout: The Long Yard
setup: Aro has never been hit in this arena. Not blocked — hit. The bout is a hundred paces of open sand and the entire question is whether you can close it.

opponent.name: Aro of the Horizon Reach
opponent._poolsDerived_20260905: health removed: it was on the retired 3-7 scale and overrode a live synthesised sheet, which made a bout end in a median of ONE turn. The pool now derives from standing (30 + 5/level) through the level the threat implies. `yieldAtFraction` replaces an absolute `yieldAt` because a ratio is scale-free.

party.ifYouBringPeople: ⛔ A HUNDRED PACES OF OPEN SAND AND MORE THAN ONE ANGLE. Aro's whole game is never being where the swing is, ⚑ AND THREE PEOPLE HAVE THREE SWINGS. ⚠️ He is beatable by a party in a way he is not beatable alone, and he knows it — he will try to make it a duel by ignoring two of you until they are out of position.
party.whatItAsksOfAParty: ⚑ Whether you can stay spread. ⛔ The instinct is to converge and converging is how he wins.
party.foldNote: A folded MOVE ally closes distance you cannot. ⚠️ It is the cell where the fold most directly answers the opponent's whole method.

_partyClauseWhy: ⛔ THE PARTY CLAUSE — R36/R36a, authored 2026-09-05. These eight were built one per contribution family to prove EVERY FAMILY CAN WIN A FIGHT, and they were written when a fight was one person against one opponent. ⚑ R36 MAKES A PARTY MEMBER FIGHT FROM THEIR OWN SHEET and R36a caps three acting fully. ⚠️ SO THE QUESTION THESE CELLS ASK IS NOW A PARTY QUESTION: not 'can a restorer win a duel' but 'what does a restorer DO when two other people are also on the sand.' ⛔ NOTHING IN THE PROSE CHANGED — the clause is additive, and it is what a GM reads when more than one person walks out.
